entry.title: Modeling Device Capabilities for Analytics
A seed-independent hash collision in GxHash
entry.summary: For a pangenome deduplication tool I’m working on (pandedup), I’m using 128-bit hashes as “unique” identifiers of substrings. Sadly, it turns out that gxhash128 (the 128-bit version of gxhash) has a hash collision between the two strings of length 88 below that only differ in 5 positions, regardless of the value of the seed. Looking at the strings, this clearly isn’t a random collision. Those could be expected when doing \(2^{64}\) lookups in a dictionary of \(2^{64}\) keys, but my data is nowhere near that large.

This week note covers the week of 21st–26th July.
Last week was quite busy with a lot of running around. In the week prior, we celebrated our now 4yo A’s birthday. Since we were never able to have a big party for A for any of her important occasions in the last four years, we decided to throw one this time. We booked a party hall and invited all her school and home friends and their parents. The party hall had a children’s play arena attached to it and all the children had great fun. The parents were probably bored making small talk to each other, but the children were running around having the time of their life. We had A cut a giant purple cake and lunch was served.
